headline: Five wins that show the world is getting better
meta_description: From Indonesia's poverty breakthrough to wildlife bridges saving lives, this week brought real reasons for hope across the globe.
summary_short: Indonesia has slashed extreme poverty by 83% in four decades, while a Colorado wildlife bridge cut animal deaths by 91%—among this week's victories.
body:
In four decades, Indonesia has lifted millions from extreme poverty in one of the world's most dramatic reversals. The share of Indonesians living on less than $3 per day plummeted from 86% in 1984 to less than 4% by 2025, according to the nonprofit Our World in Data. While China has led Asia's anti-poverty charge, Indonesia's achievement remains "impressive," with statistics showing that three million people alone escaped extreme poverty in the previous decade. Though critics note that social assistance programs like cash handouts played a role, the outcome is clear: millions of Indonesians are living more comfortably than before, marking a genuine transformation in living standards across the archipelago.

Elsewhere, infrastructure is reshaping how we coexist with nature. Colorado's new $15 million wildlife overpass—North America's largest crossing—has reduced animal-vehicle collisions by 91% since opening last December. Elk, pronghorn, and bears now safely traverse Interstate 25 through the bridge and five accompanying underpasses, turning a deadly freeway stretch into a migration corridor.

Meanwhile, London's River Thames is experiencing its own rebirth. The city's new "super sewer" has cut raw sewage entering the river by 86%, preventing 84 tonnes of litter from reaching the waterway. And in the Seychelles, Aldabra giant tortoises have bounced back from near-extinction: a survey found 180,000 individuals on the atoll—more tortoises than the archipelago's human population—compared to just 1,000 a century ago. These stories share a common thread: when humans commit to change, ecosystems and communities respond.
quick_facts: Indonesia: extreme poverty fell from 86% to under 4% in 40 years
Colorado wildlife bridge: 91% reduction in animal-vehicle collisions
Thames super sewer: 86% drop in raw sewage entering the river
Aldabra giant tortoises: 180,000 individuals, up from 1,000 in 1800s
Three million Indonesians lifted from extreme poverty in past decade alone
